name: Functional analysis
summary: Integral equations and the calculus of variations are treated as linear algebra in infinite-dimensional normed spaces with topological structure.

name: Volterra functionals
summary: Volterra introduced functionals as functions of functions, and Hadamard named the field in 1910.

name: Heaviside operational calculus
summary: Heaviside treated differentiation as an algebraic operator to solve telegraph and circuit equations, later justified through Laplace transforms.

name: Peano arithmetic axioms
summary: Dedekind and Peano gave axioms characterizing the natural numbers, Peano in formal logical notation.

name: Killing-Cartan classification
summary: Killing and Cartan decomposed semisimple Lie algebras into simple ones and classified them into four families plus exceptional cases.

name: Geometry of numbers (Minkowski)
summary: Convex bodies and lattices in R^n are used to prove existence of integer points, with consequences for quadratic forms and algebraic number fields.

name: Commutative algebra from invariant theory and ideals
summary: Non-constructive finiteness arguments for invariants and ideals of polynomials replace computation, and rings become the unit of study.

name: Italian algebraic geometry
summary: Castelnuovo, Enriques and Severi classified algebraic surfaces up to birational equivalence with geometric methods lacking rigorous foundations.

name: Lyapunov stability
summary: Lyapunov gave general criteria for stability of equilibria using auxiliary functions.

name: Biometric mathematical statistics
summary: Pearson developed correlation and chi-square for biological data and founded Biometrika.
